stops.note: possibly referring to climate or a yearly calendar of the stars
Roger Bacon used the word in the 1260s for astronomical tables; its Arabic origin is still debated
first recorded around 1392 in 'The Equatorie of the Planetis', an English astronomical treatise sometimes attributed to Chaucer
stops.meaning: an annual book of tables and forecasts

current_meaning: an annual publication with calendars, weather forecasts, and other data
